chunks: And from him, from Safwan and Fadala, from al-Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the Imams (peace be upon them both), who said:

"If a man owns his two parents, or his sister, or his paternal aunt, or his maternal aunt, they are freed (from being sold again as slaves). And he owns his son of his brother, his paternal uncle, and his maternal uncle. And he owns his paternal uncle and his maternal uncle from suckling (milk-kinship)."
ai.seo_question: What are the rules for freeing close relatives who are owned as slaves in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the principle of *kafā'ah* (kinship barrier) in manumission, distinguishing between direct ascendants/descendants who cannot be owned by the same person and collateral relatives who can. It specifically notes that uncles acquired through suckling (*radā'ah*) are treated similarly to blood uncles, thereby preventing ownership of one's own milk-uncle. This ruling reflects the Shia juristic view that close kinship ties, whether by blood or nursing, preclude the master-slave relationship to preserve familial dignity.
